title: Black Holes
blurb: Every pixel integrates a light ray through curved spacetime. See why the shadow is far larger than the horizon — and why a bigger hole is gentler to fall into.

sources.claim: null geodesic equation d²u/dφ² + u = (3/2) r_s u², u = 1/r
sources.cite: standard result of the Schwarzschild metric; see Misner, Thorne & Wheeler, Gravitation, ch. 25
sources.note: Integrated per-pixel with RK2. The (3/2)r_s u² term is the entire departure from Newtonian gravity and is what produces the photon ring.

sources.claim: accretion disk temperature profile T ∝ r^(-3/4)

sources.cite: EHT Collaboration 2019, ApJL 875, L1; 2022, ApJL 930, L12

open: Non-spinning (Schwarzschild) only. Real black holes rotate, which drags the photon ring off-centre and moves the ISCO inward — Kerr geometry is not implemented.
Doppler beaming is not applied to the accretion disk, so the real asymmetry (one side much brighter) is missing.
The disk is a thin equatorial annulus with no vertical structure or optical depth.
performance: Ray-marches a geodesic per pixel. Needs a GPU; software rendering is not viable. ?steps=N lowers the count.
